title_en: Fragments from Book 3 Against Theodore of Mopsuestia
author: Cyril of Alexandria
occasion: Cyril writes against Theodore of Mopsuestia's Christology, defending the unity of Christ against a view that separates the divine Word from the human nature.
argument: Cyril urges his opponent to grasp the depth of the mystery of Christ. He insists that while divinity and flesh are distinct in their natural properties, they must be confessed as one Son in an inseparable union. The human nature in Christ is honored and sanctified, yet as the Word he is the giver of the Spirit and did not need baptism or the Spirit for his own being. Those who think rightly will have Christ reveal to them the knowledge of the mystery concerning himself.

outline.move: Cyril opens by calling the reader to understand the depth of the mystery and to follow the aim of the sacred writings, noting that divinity and flesh are distinct in their natural properties.

He urges confessing the flesh as united to the Word without separation, so that one worships one Son who is consubstantial with the Father divinely and with us humanly; then he states that Christ will reveal the knowledge of his mystery to those who think rightly, and that the human nature in Christ is honored and sanctified, since as the Word he is the giver of the Spirit and did not need baptism or participation in the Spirit for his own existence.

This section repeats the same fragmentary material as frag-rem-early: the tail end of the consubstantiality formula, the statement about Christ revealing the mystery, and the paragraph about the human nature being honored and sanctified and the Word as giver of the Spirit.

_unresolved_facts.claim: defending the unity of Christ against a view that separates the divine Word from the human nature
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source does not explicitly describe Theodore's view as 'separating the divine Word from the human nature'; this is an inference. The source shows Cyril arguing for inseparable union but does not preserve Theodore's actual position.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Those who think rightly will have Christ reveal to them the knowledge of the mystery concerning himself
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Christ will 'turn back' or 'reverse' (ἀναστρέψει) the knowledge of the mystery to those who choose to think thus—likely meaning he will restore or give back, but the verb suggests a more active, possibly corrective action rather than simple revelation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: frag-rem-early contains: 'He urges confessing the flesh as united to the Word without separation, so that one worships one Son who is consubstantial with the Father divinely and with us humanly; then he states that Christ will reveal the knowledge of his mystery to those who think rightly, and that the human nature in Christ is honored and sanctified, since as the Word he is the giver of the Spirit and did not need baptism or participation in the Spirit for his own existence.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: πλὴν ἀπόδος αὐτῷ καθ' ἕνωσιν ἀδιάσπαστον τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ, μὴ ἀπογυμνώσῃς αὐτὸν τοῦ καταπετάσματος
_unresolved_facts.fix: The opening of frag-rem-early begins mid-sentence with 'πλὴν' (nevertheless/however) and the imperative 'ἀπόδος' (give back/return), indicating this is a continuation from lost material, not a fresh start. The brief should note the fragmentary nature more clearly.

_unresolved_facts.claim: frag-rem-mid repeats the same fragmentary material as frag-rem-early
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source text for frag-rem-mid and frag-rem-close is IDENTICAL to frag-rem-early, not merely 'the same fragmentary material.' These appear to be exact duplicates of the same fragment, not independent witnesses. The brief should state they are verbatim repetitions of the same text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: frag-rem-close repeats the same fragmentary material as frag-rem-early and frag-rem-mid
_unresolved_facts.fix: Same issue: these are verbatim identical texts, not summaries of repeated material. The source shows three sections with exactly the same content.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Theodore of Mopsuestia, whose Christology Cyril refutes
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐκ τοῦ πρὸς τὰ Θεοδώρου ἐπισκόπου Μοψουεστίας τρίτου λόγου
_unresolved_facts.fix: Theodore is named only in the title as the dedicatee/opponent ('πρὸς τὰ Θεοδώρου'). He does not appear as a speaking voice or directly addressed figure in the surviving fragments. The brief should note he is the named opponent in the title only.

_unresolved_facts.claim: First-person plural and direct address to the opponent
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἌΚΟΥΕ τοίνυν καὶ πρὸς ἡμῶν Σύνες ἄνθρωπε τοῦ μυστηρίου τὸ βάθος
_unresolved_facts.fix: The first-person plural 'πρὸς ἡμῶν' means 'from us' (i.e., 'hear from us'), not a first-person plural verb form. The direct address uses second-person singular imperatives (ἌΚΟΥΕ, Σύνες) to 'ἄνθρωπε' (O man), not specifically to Theodore. The 'how_marked' should be 'second-person singular imperative address to an unnamed interlocutor ('O man').'

The voice in frag-rem-early, frag-rem-mid, and frag-rem-close is not clearly marked as Cyril's by first-person forms; these fragments contain no first-person markers. The voice attribution should be limited to frag-open where 'πρὸς ἡμῶν' appears, or marked as 'unmarked, presumably Cyril' for the other fragments.
